reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, the resource assessment rubric, the fresh-review framework, the resource-review context, the full ImmunizationRecommendation StructureDefinition report, the direct SearchParameters and HttpRestBehavior behavior findings, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. I used the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level conclusion. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context because the assigned resource is not Resource or DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ImmunizationRecommendation is trial-use/FMM 1, so there is weak formal stability pressure and removal is easier to justify than it would be for mature or normative content. That does not erase the domain concern: the resource carries patient-specific immunization forecasting, including due/overdue/immune/contraindicated status, date criteria, and supporting evidence, so public-health and clinical reminder workflows can still face meaningful migration risk.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 core removes the ImmunizationRecommendation resource, so migration is already a resource/endpoint/search redesign problem; local compatibility still matters mainly through resource-retention, transition aliases, terminology retention, and explicit mapping guidance.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual migration shape is not a handful of local element edits. R4 has a concrete `ImmunizationRecommendation` resource, while the checked R6 package has no same-name resource definition or index entry. Existing R4 instances therefore fail at `resourceType` before any child-path migration is considered, generated model and REST surfaces disappear, and there is no evident computable successor map in the local package.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The R4 resource's central `recommendation` backbone is mandatory and repeatable and carries the forecast payload: vaccine or target disease, mandatory modifier `forecastStatus`, date criteria, dose/series details, contraindicated vaccine options, and supporting evidence. R6 has adjacent immunization and workflow concepts, but the reports do not show a one-to-one R6 replacement that preserves a point-in-time forecast snapshot. A real migration program must choose a target pattern, such as retaining R4 at a boundary, profiling R6 workflow resources plus extensions, or preserving snapshots in implementation-specific structures.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the resource identity is gone, preventing one more child-element or terminology break has reduced standalone value once the broader redesign is accepted. The high-leverage compatibility question is whether to preserve the resource identity or provide transition behavior and official mappings. If the standards decision is to remove the resource, the local backbone and forecast-status terminology changes become migration chores inside that larger program, not independent reasons that each old path must survive.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most meaningful less-breaking base option would be to keep `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a deprecated or legacy trial-use R6 resource while documenting the preferred R6 workflow approach. That could preserve old instances, generated APIs, search endpoints, and the forecasting backbone, but it has real maintenance and dual-model costs. Lower-cost mitigations that still matter include retired/deprecated recommendation terminology artifacts, ConceptMaps, explicit endpoint/search transition guidance, and optional implementation aliases or redirects; those help migration even though maps and local aliases are not themselves base compatibility preservation.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The two direct behavior findings are in scope and reinforce the same shape. The removed-resource search-surface finding means old `ImmunizationRecommendation?...` queries lose their R6 endpoint/search base, and the HTTP REST inventory finding means the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises the endpoint. Both are derivative of resource removal rather than independent behavior redesigns. OperationDefinitions had no direct ImmunizationRecommendation finding in the reviewed context. The eleven shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may affect generic clients but are not scored against this resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Yes`, `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and `migration-program-dominates`; I agree with that core conclusion after independently checking the resource and behavior evidence. I would frame the consequence more narrowly: migration-program dominance should not be read as 'no point preserving anything.' It means the main standards-review issue is the resource lifecycle and transition plan, while terminology retention, aliases, and maps remain useful low-cost mitigations.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high that the resource is absent from the checked R6 ballot package and that R4 instances cannot validate as R6 core. Confidence is lower about the standards intent, final successor pattern, and implementation prevalence because the local inputs do not include an official removal rationale or cross-version map.

findingConsiderations.title: ImmunizationRecommendation resource is absent from the R6 ballot core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive break. A valid R4 instance with `resourceType: "ImmunizationRecommendation"` has no R6 core StructureDefinition/type to validate against, and the generated class, parser branch, REST endpoint, and search base disappear. Low FMM weakens the stability claim, but vaccine forecasting is public-health and clinical reminder content, so the removal remains standards-review-worthy.

findingConsiderations.title: The local R4 forecasting content model has no same-resource R6 element set
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The removed backbone is the resource's core forecast model, not an incidental property. Its mandatory repeatable structure and modifier `forecastStatus` carry due/overdue/immune/contraindicated semantics and timing criteria. This confirms that migration is policy-bearing and lossy unless the resource or an explicit successor representation is provided.

findingConsiderations.title: No computable R6 replacement mapping was found; migration to related workflow resources is lossy
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The absence of a local successor map changes this from a mechanical rename into a migration program. Implementers must decide how to represent forecast status, date criteria, contraindications, and supporting evidence in R6 patterns, with clinical reminder and audit consequences if mappings diverge.

findingConsiderations.title: Recommendation-specific terminology bindings and status code system are not present in the checked R6 package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This matters for enum generation, terminology caches, stricter profiles, and business logic around statuses such as `overdue`, `immune`, and `contraindicated`, but it is not the main base instance-validity break because the R4 binding was example-strength and the containing resource/path is already removed. Retiring or carrying forward the terminology with ConceptMaps is a useful mitigation rather than a reason by itself to preserve every old element path.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For ImmunizationRecommendation this is a direct client-visible break: old endpoint searches have no same R6 resource base. It is derivative of resource removal, so the right review target is the resource lifecycle and successor query guidance, not a separate per-parameter rescue in isolation.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The endpoint inventory change confirms that generic clients and conformance tools lose the advertised ImmunizationRecommendation REST surface. The break matters operationally, but compatibility aliases or redirects only make sense if the standards lifecycle decision keeps or explicitly transitions the removed resource model.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This and the other shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may affect generic Resource clients, but they are not specific to ImmunizationRecommendation and should not be double-counted as evidence for this resource's migration shape.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Make the standards lifecycle decision explicit: either retain `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a deprecated/legacy R6 resource for transition, or publish a clear rationale and replacement pattern for immunization forecasting.

Provide migration guidance or a computable map for forecast status, date criteria, vaccine/target-disease choices, contraindicated vaccine options, dose/series data, and supporting evidence, including expected R6 endpoint and search behavior.

If the resource remains removed, carry recommendation-specific CodeSystem/ValueSet artifacts forward as retired/deprecated terminology or publish ConceptMaps so validators, terminology services, and business-rule code have a stable transition target.
Document whether servers may expose compatibility endpoints, redirects, or CapabilityStatement aliases for legacy ImmunizationRecommendation searches, and what conformance status such behavior has.

caveats: The local R6 package proves absence of the core resource in the checked ballot package, but not the work group's full rationale or intended final replacement.
R4 FMM 1/trial-use reduces the baseline compatibility burden, so production prevalence should not be assumed from maturity alone.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context and not as resource-specific breaks.
